source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The new docs say the outer Option tracks whether a member is present. That is a state the Rust value can express, but the emitted ordinary nested-Option decoder does not preserve it for JSON null: serde_json calls visit_none on the outer Option, which returns None. The generator adds default and skip_serializing_none, not a double-option deserializer. The changed user test expects explicit null fields through ..Default::default(). Outgoing None is omitted, Some(None) emits null and Some(Some(value)) emits a value. Narrow the documentation to distinguish these outgoing states from input decoding, and add direct null-versus-omitted coverage if that input distinction is intended. This conclusion uses paired local dependency code, not a fresh execution or a global Serde style rule.
title: Graph nullable fields preserve outgoing states but collapse null on input
